title: Routine donor-specific transplant tolerance without lifelong immunosuppression

concept.text: The innovation would make a recipient’s immune system durably accept a transplanted donor organ without lifelong maintenance immunosuppression. Acceptance would be donor-specific: immune responses against the graft would be restrained while useful responses against infections, cancer and unrelated antigens remained functional. Achieving this routinely across mismatched donors and different organs, without intensive immune-system ablation, remains the proposed capability.

The central problem spans both existing immune cells and cells produced after transplantation. Teaching developing T cells to tolerate donor antigens could reduce future alloreactivity, but established memory populations can persist independently of new thymic output. A successful treatment therefore needs durable control of donor-directed immunity across these populations. Thymic donor-antigen expression and donor hematopoietic chimerism are relevant approaches, rather than defining requirements for every possible solution.

significance.text: Reliable tolerance would change the long-term bargain of transplantation by removing dependence on continual immunosuppressive treatment. Pettigrew’s January 2025 account links that treatment to heightened infection and cancer risks. Safely eliminating the dependence could substantially improve transplant care, but preserved protective immunity must be demonstrated; it cannot be inferred merely from graft survival.

The capability could also support donor-derived cell and tissue replacement. The reviewed article describes human embryonic stem-cell survival and multilineage expression in humanized mice, providing a preclinical connection to regenerative medicine. Extending tolerance to clinically useful replacement tissues would require separate demonstrations of immune acceptance, tissue function and safety.

Impact assessment: donor-specific tolerance would address an important immune barrier to transplantation, but would not itself increase organ supply or prevent every nonimmune cause of graft failure. The analogy to teaching the immune system that a donor organ is acceptable is useful only if acceptance remains selective and durable. Broad immune impairment could also permit graft survival, without delivering the intended breakthrough.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is reliable, durable donor-specific tolerance without the substantial morbidity of intensive conditioning and immune reconstitution. Recipients may encounter multiple mismatched donor major histocompatibility complex antigens. A practical strategy must address that diversity sufficiently to prevent rejection, rather than demonstrate acceptance only under a narrowly controlled antigenic configuration.

A key biological barrier is the distinction between shaping developing T cells and controlling established immunity. Expressing donor antigens in the thymus can influence newly developing cells, but persistent memory populations may remain capable of attacking the graft. The article’s contrast between naive mice maintained under pathogen-free conditions and the challenge of persistent human memory cells limits how directly the mouse results can predict clinical performance.

For a thymic gene-delivery approach, donor-MHC expression must become a clinically usable intervention rather than remain a controlled experimental manipulation. The human-cell experiments described in the review involved transduced fetal thymic tissue in humanized mice. Separately, selected human tolerance experiences involving donor hematopoietic stem cells required aggressive conditioning. Neither setting establishes a routine method that combines effective donor-antigen presentation, control of existing alloreactivity and an acceptable treatment burden.

Engineering synthesis: a deployable treatment would need reproducible delivery, adequate persistence of the tolerizing effect and a way to establish that immune protection remains intact. It would also need evidence that tolerance survives clinically relevant immune challenges. These are proposed translation requirements; the supplied material does not identify a validated implementation that satisfies them together.

current_state.text: Geoffrey Pettigrew’s research highlight, “Intrathymic alloantigen expression—the Holy Grail or reinventing the wheel?”, was published on 6 January 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41422-024-01067-3. It describes mouse experiments in which donor-MHC expression in recipient thymic epithelial cells preceded donor-strain skin transplantation by two months. The reported grafts survived long term without provoking donor-directed alloantibody responses. The supplied review does not provide an exact duration for that long-term survival, so it cannot support a numerical durability claim.

Experiments involving human cells were performed in humanized mice, not human transplant recipients. The article describes survival and multilineage expression of third-party human embryonic stem cells in a setting involving transduced fetal thymic tissue. This is a preclinical result relevant to cell replacement; it does not demonstrate clinical thymic tolerance induction, functional organ replacement or preserved human protective immunity.

The article separately discusses immunosuppression-free organ survival in selected human recipients, generally using aggressive conditioning and donor hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation to establish chimerism. These experiences demonstrate meaningful clinical progress, while leaving the conditioning burden unresolved. The article’s opening assessment specifically concerns the difficulty of obtaining long-term immunosuppression-free clinical graft survival without intense myeloablative conditioning; it does not assert that immunosuppression-free transplantation has never occurred.

The evidence supplied here is a research highlight reporting other work. The validated review records complete, identity-verified HTML and PDF extractions without extraction problems, but the underlying Liu study was not supplied or independently inspected. Consequently, the experimental details above rest on secondary reporting. The account establishes what was reported in January 2025; the empty freshness record does not establish the field’s status as of 1 November 2026 or whether subsequent work has changed it.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration: randomized, multicenter studies would show years of sustained graft function after withdrawal of maintenance immunosuppression, without intensive immune-system ablation. Studies should include multiple organ types and meaningfully mismatched donors, with transparent accounting of unsuccessful withdrawal, rejection, rescue treatment and conditioning-related harm. These are proposed criteria for convincing evidence, not established consensus thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Years of sustained graft function after maintenance immunosuppression withdrawal

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration of specificity: clinical outcomes and immune testing would jointly show restrained donor-directed responses alongside preserved responses to third-party antigens and infections. Protective immunity against cancer would require appropriate evidence and follow-up rather than inference from short-term immune assays. Challenge protocols would need explicit definitions and an ethically appropriate clinical design; intentional exposure to dangerous infections is not required.
completion_criteria.label: Donor-directed responses restrained while third-party and protective immunity remain functional

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration of durability and reproducibility: independent centers would reproduce the effect in recipients with varied immune histories, and follow-up would test whether tolerance persists through immune-cell turnover and clinically relevant immune challenges. Results should define the donor mismatches, organs, recipient characteristics and treatment conditions for which success has been demonstrated. Finite studies can establish breadth within those boundaries, not literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Independent centers reproduce durable tolerance within defined clinical boundaries

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: the complete treatment course, including induction, monitoring and any rescue therapy, would need an acceptable balance of benefit and harm compared with maintenance immunosuppression. A protocol whose initial conditioning or lasting immune impairment outweighs the benefit of drug withdrawal would not fulfill the intended routine clinical capability.
completion_criteria.label: Complete treatment shows acceptable benefit–harm balance versus maintenance immunosuppression

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: IMM-04, durable antigen-specific reversal of established autoimmunity, shares the goal of selectively restraining harmful immunity while preserving useful defenses. IMM-05 concerns responses to donor tissue; IMM-04 concerns established responses against the recipient’s own tissues. IMM-11, causal mechanisms initiating the breakdown of self-tolerance, addresses the origins of self-directed immunity rather than establishing acceptance of a transplant.

Roster-based synthesis: IMM-01, a general decoder for T-cell antigen recognition, could help characterize donor-reactive T cells, while IMM-02, a predictive causal theory of whole immune responses, could help explain when tolerance persists or fails. Recognition prediction and whole-system explanation are distinct capabilities from a treatment that actually produces durable transplant acceptance.

Roster-based synthesis: IMM-09, in-body programming of immune cells, overlaps with the possibility of directly modifying immune behavior to induce tolerance. Thymic gene delivery is a relevant connection, but IMM-05 does not require a particular programming platform. IMM-08, restoration of youthful immune competence, overlaps through thymic function and immune renewal; improved competence alone does not establish donor-specific acceptance.

Roster-based synthesis: IMM-03, directed evolution of broadly protective vaccine antibodies; IMM-06, immune eradication of heterogeneous solid tumors; and IMM-07, treatment-free immune control of established HIV infection, concern protective responses that transplant tolerance should preserve. They require their own positive demonstrations of protection or disease control. Successful donor tolerance would not establish any of those capabilities.

Roster-based synthesis: IMM-10, real-time control of life-threatening systemic inflammation, concerns acute inflammatory control rather than durable donor-specific acceptance. IMM-12, programmable trained immunity; IMM-13, causal control of microbiome–immune interactions; and IMM-14, bidirectional control of neuroimmune circuits, concern other routes of immune regulation. Possible interactions with graft acceptance do not make these entries interchangeable, and the supplied evidence does not establish any of them as prerequisites for IMM-05.

unresolved_issues: The field’s status as of 1 November 2026 remains unverified because the supplied freshness record is empty.

The underlying Liu study was not supplied or independently inspected; its full methods, sample sizes, controls, exact graft-survival duration and reproducibility cannot be established from this record.
The supplied evidence does not establish whether thymic donor-antigen expression can durably control persistent human alloreactive memory populations without intensive conditioning.
Clinical delivery requirements, acceptable induction burden and the donor and organ settings in which a practical protocol would work remain unresolved.
Operational definitions of tolerance, follow-up duration, immune-challenge protocols and adequate evidence of preserved infection and cancer protection require specification in actual studies.

brief.title: Organ transplants without lifelong anti-rejection drugs
possible: People receiving a donor organ could live without lifelong drugs that suppress their immune system. Their immune system would accept the organ while keeping its ability to fight infections and cancer. This would become a routine option across different organs and donors, without treatment that extensively destroys immune cells.
why: For transplant recipients, freedom from continual immune-suppressing treatment could reduce the heightened infection and cancer risks that accompany it. The same ability to accept donor tissue could also help people receive replacement cells and tissues.

sources.who: Gavin J. Pettigrew, discussing Liu and colleagues
sources.showed: Pettigrew describes Liu and colleagues teaching developing immune cells in mice to accept donor tissue. Donor skin survived long term without antibodies attacking it. Related experiments supported human stem-cell survival in mice carrying human immune tissue.
sources.quote: Donor strain skin allografts transplanted two months later did not provoke alloantibody responses in the recipient and survived long term.
sources.cited_for: Animal experiments support teaching developing immune cells to accept donor tissue.
sources.not_established: These experiments leave open whether the approach can control adults’ existing donor-reactive immune cells safely.

sources.showed: In a small randomized trial, 75% of treated kidney recipients reached the endpoint of remaining off immune-suppressing drugs for years. All received kidneys from closely matched living siblings, plus donor cells, radiation and immune-targeting treatment.
sources.quote: Twenty recipients received the MDR-101 infusion, and none developed graft versus host disease.
sources.cited_for: A randomized trial demonstrated sustained drug withdrawal and improved quality of life in selected kidney recipients.
sources.not_established: Routine success across mismatched donors and other organs, with an acceptable overall treatment burden, remains to be demonstrated.

sources.showed: A small kidney-transplant study reported 26 recipients off immune-suppressing drugs without rejection. Donor blood-forming cells persisted alongside recipients’ cells. The researchers also evaluated responses to vaccination.
sources.quote:
Persistently chimeric patients retained chimerism 
after removal of IS and remained rejection free without donor HLA–specific antibody development.
sources.cited_for: Selected kidney recipients maintained drug-free acceptance, with evidence of vaccine responses.
sources.not_established: The study leaves broad protection against infection and cancer, and the overall benefit–harm balance, unresolved.

sources.showed: A small study combined kidney and bone marrow transplants from related donors with mismatched immune-recognition markers. Most recipients stopped immune-suppressing drugs and maintained kidney function. Serious complications included irreversible rejection.
sources.cited_for: Drug-free kidney survival and selective restraint of donor-directed immune responses have been demonstrated in selected people.
sources.not_established: The small study leaves the safety and reliability of wider use unresolved.

shown: The MDR-101-MLK Study Group demonstrated years of drug-free kidney survival in a small randomized trial involving closely matched siblings. Leventhal and colleagues reported longer drug-free follow-up in selected kidney recipients. These treatments combined organ transplantation with donor blood-forming cells and preparatory immune treatment.

Liu and colleagues achieved long-term donor-skin survival in mice by teaching developing immune cells to accept donor markers. Adult humans also carry long-lived immune cells that may still attack a donor organ.
missing: A routine treatment must work across substantially mismatched donors and different organs without extensively destroying immune cells.
Treatment must control existing donor-reactive immune cells as well as newly developing ones.
Long-term studies must demonstrate preserved protection against infection and cancer alongside donor acceptance.
The complete treatment must offer an acceptable balance of benefit and harm compared with lifelong immune-suppressing drugs.

milestones.label: Years of organ function after drug withdrawal
milestones.explanation: Randomized trials across centers would show years of organ function after drug withdrawal, across organs and mismatched donors without extensive immune-cell destruction. Accounting for failures and harm would establish reliability.

milestones.label: Donor acceptance with protective immunity intact
milestones.explanation: Clinical outcomes and immune tests would show restrained donor responses alongside responses to unrelated targets and infections, with cancer protection assessed over time. This would establish selective acceptance.

milestones.label: Independent centers reproduce lasting acceptance
milestones.explanation: Independent centers would reproduce acceptance across varied immune histories, through immune-cell replacement and relevant immune challenges. Results would define the donors, organs and recipients for whom treatment works.

milestones.label: The complete treatment has an acceptable safety balance
milestones.explanation: The full course, including preparation, monitoring and rescue treatment, would show an acceptable benefit–harm balance against lifelong immune-suppressing drugs. This would establish its suitability for routine care.

uncertain: Can teaching newly developing immune cells to accept donor tissue also overcome adults’ persistent donor-reactive immune memory?
Which donor differences, organs and recipient immune histories can a practical treatment accommodate?
How much follow-up and which immune tests would establish durable acceptance and preserved infection and cancer protection?

page.title: Donor-specific organ transplant tolerance
page.definition: A treatment makes an organ recipient accept donor tissue without maintenance immunosuppression or myeloablative conditioning, which destroys blood-forming marrow cells. Acceptance is donor-specific: immune responses to unrelated antigens remain functional.

goal.need: Chronic immunosuppression contributes to cancer after transplantation. A US registry-linkage study covering 175,732 solid-organ transplants during 1987–2008 found an excess cancer incidence of 719.3 cases per 100,000 person-years. These observational data establish a burden associated with transplantation, but do not quantify the reduction achievable through tolerance induction.

figures.caption: Cancer outcomes in the US Transplant Cancer Match cohort
figures.note: The incidence ratio compares observed cancers with those expected from general-population rates.

statements.context: The programme solicited studies of safety, toxicity and efficacy in nonhuman-primate kidney and islet transplantation.

statements.quote: in the absence of generalized immunosuppression with concurrent immunocompetence to non-donor antigens.
statements.context: The network's clinical objective also requires clinical, laboratory and histological evidence of normal or stable organ-graft function.

completion.title: FDA licenses a donor-specific tolerance treatment permitting complete maintenance-drug withdrawal.
completion.criterion: FDA issues a biologics licence for a treatment whose approved indication is induction of donor-specific organ-transplant tolerance, with a regimen permitting complete withdrawal of maintenance immunosuppression without myeloablative conditioning. Achievement is restricted to the organ, donor–recipient human leukocyte antigen relationship and treatment regimen in the approved label. Each organ case requires an authorised indication.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, general biologics-licensure requirements in 21 CFR 601.4(a); the approved label determines the permitted indication and regimen.
completion.threshold_quote: the establishment(s) and the product meet the applicable requirements established in this chapter.
completion.basis: Licensure supplies an external decision about clinical use of the complete product and regimen. The FDA rule does not prescribe a tolerance-specific success percentage or follow-up duration. Drug-free graft function in selected research participants does not establish a licensed indication. No qualifying product was located in FDA's cellular-therapy list or approval searches through 14 November 2026.

milestones.title: A rodent retains a graft over 100 days, accepts second donor grafts and rejects unrelated grafts.
milestones.criterion: The conventional rodent test combines graft survival for more than 100 days, acceptance of a second graft from the original donor strain and rejection of unrelated-donor grafts without maintenance immunosuppression. In 2025, Liu and colleagues reported donor-skin survival to day 100 and unrelated-skin rejection on days 6–15; the principal skin-graft comparisons used six independent experiments per group. This supports the mechanism but does not establish kidney or liver attainment of the complete test.
milestones.set_by: Experimental transplantation community; the rodent convention is documented by Salama and colleagues in 2001. Its duration is not a clinical durability criterion.
milestones.threshold_quote: more than 100 days in rodents, with acceptance of a second graft from the original donor strain and rejection of third-party grafts

milestones.title: A human organ recipient completes planned immunosuppression withdrawal while retaining graft function.
milestones.criterion: A recipient treated in a human tolerance-induction study stops all maintenance immunosuppression while the transplanted organ continues functioning. Kidney: Kawai and colleagues reported withdrawal in four of five recipients of mismatched related-donor kidneys and marrow in 2008; one recipient developed irreversible humoral rejection. Liver: Todo and colleagues reported successful withdrawal in seven of ten living-donor recipients given a regulatory-T-cell-enriched product in 2016; three developed rejection during withdrawal.
milestones.set_by: Immune Tolerance Network, published primary objective for interventional transplantation studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: complete and planned withdrawal of all immunosuppression while maintaining the healthy function of the graft organ.

milestones.title: An organ graft functions without histological rejection for at least one year off immunosuppression.
milestones.criterion: Operational tolerance requires a functioning graft without histological rejection, no immunosuppressive drugs for at least one year and an immunocompetent recipient. Kidney: the 2023 FCR001 report described 26 of 37 recipients off drugs for 36–123 months, with normal biopsies; vaccine responses were measured in subsets. Liver: the 2025 LIFT report found that 13 of 80 recipients beginning withdrawal met its 12-month histological criteria. LIFT assessed spontaneous tolerance rather than tolerance induction.
milestones.set_by: Clinical transplantation community; the definition covering kidney and liver transplantation is reproduced by Page, Dar and Knechtle in 2012.
milestones.threshold_quote: in the absence of any immunosuppressive drugs (for at least 1 year), in an immunocompetent host

milestones.title: Recipients in a randomised organ-transplant study remain off all immunosuppression for over two years.
milestones.criterion: Recipients reach the published drug-free endpoint in a multicentre randomised comparison of tolerance induction with standard treatment. Kidney: in the 2025 MDR-101 study, 15 of 20 treated recipients reached more than two years off immunosuppression; ten controls received standard treatment. Donors were two-haplotype-matched siblings, and conditioning used antithymocyte globulin and ten fractions of lymphoid irradiation. Liver: four of ten recipients in Todo's uncontrolled pilot exceeded 24 months off drugs; this does not establish the randomised milestone.
milestones.set_by: MDR-101-MLK Study Group, phase 3 study NCT03363945. The published endpoint was set for HLA-matched living-donor kidney transplantation.
milestones.threshold_quote: Fifteen (75%) reached the primary study endpoint of IS-free for >2 years.

not_found: No universal published success rate, follow-up duration or conditioning-intensity limit was located for tolerance induction across organs and donor mismatches.
No corresponding randomised phase 3 liver tolerance-induction result was located.
The MDR-101 paper's full text was inaccessible; its abstract and institutional publication record were available.
EMA's solid-organ immunosuppressant guideline and FDA's kidney-endpoint workshop PDF could not be read.
